MACT, XVI ADDITIONAL JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES,
BENGALURU [SCCH-14], PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.624,000/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.

3. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered soft tissue loss of right forehead, CT brain show left fronto parietal EDH, thin SDH, lincer undisplaced fracture of left squaman part of temporal bone, greater wing of sphenoid and left zygoma, spinal injury, power decreased-both limbs, MRI of spine shows C3/4, C4/5 tramatic IVDP with card contusion, tenderness, swelling and deformity over right leg, fracture of both bones of right leg and abrasions over both elbows.

4. The evidence on record indicates that Orthopedic surgeon, who was examined as PW-2 has stated that the claimant has suffered 20.7% disability to particular limb and the Neurosurgeon, who was examined as PW-3 has stated that the claimant has suffered neurological disability of 23.7%.
In my view, having regard to the nature of injuries, it would be appropriate to determine the whole body disability at 20% as against 10% determined by the Tribunal.
5. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.8,000/-.
The evidence on record indicates that the claimant was a student studying Diploma in Civil Engineering.
In that view of the matter, notional income of Rs.9,500/- as per KSLSA chart cannot be applied.
Considering that the claimant was a Diploma student, it would be appropriate to determine the income at Rs.13,000/- per month.
6. As the claimant was aged 19 years, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied.

Since the whole body disability is determined at 20%, the claimant is entitled for addition of 40% of the income K Manjunath vs The Manager on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104948504/
2 towards future prospects, which would be Rs.18,200/- (13,000+40%).
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.786,240/- (18,200 x 12 x 18 x 20%) towards 'loss of future income' .
7. Having regard to the nature of injuries and length of stay in the hospital, the laid up has to be treated as 4 months instead of 2 months determined by the Tribunal.
As a consequence, the amount of Rs.16,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.52,000/- (13000 X 4 months).
8. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.50,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

9. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.30,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

10. Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the claimant would also be entitled to 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' at Rs.40,000/- as against the sum of Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
11. The sums awarded as 'medical expenses' and 'future medical expenses' by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence, does not call for modification and hence confirmed.
12. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
As As  awarded awarded

Compensation under  by the by this  different Heads  Tribunal Court  (Rs.) (Rs.)
 Pain and sufferings 50,000 75,000  Loss of future income 172,800 786,240

Medical expenses 310,000 310,000  Future medical 20,000 20,000  expenses  Loss of income during 16,000 52,000  the laid up period  Conveyance, food, 25,000 40,000  nourishment, attendant K Manjunath vs The Manager on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104948504/
3  charges  Loss of amenities in life 30,000 75,000  Total 623,800 13,58,240 13.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.13,58,240/- as against Rs.623,800/-, along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

14. It is made clear that the enhanced amount shall carry interest at 6% p.a.
15.
The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
16. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
